facts.claim: KoRo (Berlin clean-label snacking/dry-goods DTC-and-retail brand) extended its Series C by €5m from Kharis Capital on Feb 27, 2025, bringing the round (initially €35m, led by Coefficient Capital in Nov 2024) to €40m total.
NutriUnited, a German buy-and-build platform for family-owned organic/artisan food producers, raised an €8.5M seed round in November 2025 to scale its consolidation model.

Bio Company, Germany's 3rd-largest organic supermarket chain, reported FY2025 revenue of roughly €199M, essentially flat versus €201M the prior year, shortly before merging with wholesaler Terra Naturkost.
At Biofach 2026 (Feb 2026), organic F&B industry leaders warned the segment faces consolidation pressure and eroding price premiums, saying brands must "innovate and co-operate or disappear."

Growth investors Coefficient Capital (lead) and Kharis Capital backed KoRo's extended Series C (€35m Nov 2024, +€5m Feb 2025, totaling €40m), showing continued specialist-fund appetite for DACH clean-label snacking brands.

NutriUnited's €8.5M seed round (Nov 2025) drew a syndicate of German angel/family-office investors (incl. Atlantis Ventures, G-FUND, OakHorizon) specifically to fund buy-and-build acquisitions of family-owned food producers.

active_funds.name: Kharis Capital (Kharis Food Tech Fund)
active_funds.evidence: Invested €5m into KoRo's Series C extension, closed Feb 27, 2025, taking the round to €40m total.

active_funds.name: Coefficient Capital
active_funds.evidence: Led KoRo's €35m Series C (Nov 2024); the fund is known for early bets on Oatly, Just Spices and Magic Spoon, i.e. clean-label/better-for-you consumer brands.

facts.claim: Germany made the stricter Nutri-Score 2023 algorithm mandatory for all voluntary users from January 2026 (after a two-year transition ending end-2025); use of the label itself remains voluntary.

Germany's proposed Kinderlebensmittel-Werbegesetz (ad ban on high sugar/fat/salt foods aimed at under-14s) remains politically blocked as of 2025, with the BMEL's 4th draft criticized by coalition SPD lawmakers as "unworkable," repeatedly delaying the legislation.

German Agriculture Minister Alois Rainer (CSU) proposed cutting federal GAK co-financing (which covers organic-farming/agri-environmental subsidies) by €150M for 2026, creating funding uncertainty for organic producers.
Big CPG strategics (Nestlé, Danone, Mars, Kraft Heinz among others) are stepping up bolt-on M&A in health-forward, premium and better-for-you food categories heading into 2026.

dm expanded its dm Bio private-label certifications to include Bioland (from April 2026), joining existing Demeter and Naturland partnerships, becoming the first German drugstore to work with all three leading organic associations.
Dr. Oetker is pursuing "selective bolt-on opportunities in desserts and better-for-you segments" to complement organic growth, alongside its July 2025 acquisition of Kathi.

Nestlé and Danone both moved to fully own/acquire meal-replacement and functional-nutrition brands in 2026 (Yfood and Huel respectively), signaling strategic appetite for clean-label functional nutrition adjacent to organic CPG.

players.name: dm
players.evidence: CEO Kerstin Erbe: dm aims to "offer customers a bio food assortment in the best specialist retail quality," adding Bioland certification to ~700 dm Bio products alongside Demeter and Naturland (April 2026).

players.name: Dr. Oetker
players.evidence: Pursuing "selective bolt-on opportunities in desserts and better-for-you segments to complement organic growth"; acquired baking/frozen-cake maker Kathi in July 2025.

players.name: Nestlé
players.evidence: Completed full buyout of ready-to-drink meal brand Yfood in June 2026, after taking a 49.95% stake for ~€215M in 2023.

players.name: Danone
players.evidence: Agreed to acquire UK functional-nutrition/meal-replacement brand Huel for approximately €1 billion in 2026.

players.name: Katjes International
players.evidence: Acquired better-for-you snacking brand Graze (Nature Delivered Ltd) from Unilever in February 2026, adding to a portfolio strategy of acquiring growth consumer brands.

facts.claim: Holle baby food, a Swiss-based organic/biodynamic baby-food brand also distributed in Germany, was acquired/received a majority strategic investment from Spain's MaserGrup on June 23, 2025.

Bio Company and Terra Naturkost, Germany's #3 organic supermarket chain and #3 organic wholesaler, merged operations into new holding Bioverbund SE in January 2026 amid margin pressure from discounters.
Dr. Oetker acquired German baking-mix and frozen-cake maker Kathi in July 2025 as part of a bolt-on M&A strategy in desserts and better-for-you categories.
Nestlé completed a full buyout of ready-to-drink meal brand Yfood in June 2026, after first taking a 49.95% stake for roughly €215M in 2023.

Danone agreed to acquire UK meal-replacement/functional-nutrition brand Huel for approximately €1 billion in 2026, underscoring strategic buyer appetite for clean-label functional nutrition brands adjacent to this segment.

Germany's organic specialty retail sector (Naturkostfachhandel) is described as being in a consolidation phase, with smaller and mid-size chains pursuing strategic cooperations, shop-in-shop concepts, and generational ownership transitions rather than standalone growth.

players.name: Bioverbund SE (Bio Company + Terra Naturkost)
players.evidence: Germany's 3rd-largest organic supermarket chain (Bio Company, ~€199M FY revenue) merged operations with the 3rd-largest organic wholesaler (Terra Naturkost) under new holding Bioverbund SE in Jan 2026 to bundle purchasing volume and compete with discounters/drugstores on price.

players.name: NutriUnited
players.evidence: Buy-and-build platform explicitly targeting family-owned German food producers in meat, meat-alternatives and ready-meals for succession solutions; raised €8.5M seed (Nov 2025) to accelerate integrating additional family businesses (already owns Grasmehr and Morawitzky, 140+ employees).

players.name: MaserGrup
players.evidence: Spanish food group described as "eyeing M&A amid sales push" took a strategic stake/majority in Swiss-German organic baby-food brand Holle in June 2025 as part of a multi-year international buy-and-build investment plan.
